records.summary: The SMART (Multisectoral Strategic Action on Food Security and Protection for Strengthening Resilience) Project is an integrated resilience and protection initiative implemented by AVSI Foundation and Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO) in Dadaab and Fafi Sub-Counties of Garissa County. The project seeks to strengthen the resilience of refugee and host communities while improving access to essential protection services for women, children, refugees, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable populations affected by protracted displacement, poverty, protection risks and recurrent climate-related shocks. Under Outcome 2, the project aims to strengthen community-based protection systems and improve access to quality protection services through a combination of capacity strengthening, referral system enhancement, community mobilization, awareness raising, and stakeholder engagement. The intervention is grounded in a prevention and response approach that seeks to strengthen community awareness of rights, available services, protection risks and reporting mechanisms while promoting positive social norms, inclusion, accountability and social cohesion. records.title: A consultant for community based climate resilience through integrated climate change adaptation disaster risk reduction early warning & systems
records.summary: REQUEST FOR CONSULTANTS The Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) is a global humanitarian organization with a mission to work with people in poverty and distress to create just and positive changes. ADRA Somalia belongs to the worldwide network, comprised of more than 130 supporting and implementing country offices. ADRA Somalia is seeking to recruit a consultant for strengthening community-based climate resilience through integrated climate change, adaptation disaster risk reduction, early warning and systems and anticipatory action. Somalia continues to face multiple and interconnected challenges, including protracted conflict, recurrent droughts and floods, displacement, environmental degradation, poverty, and increasing pressure on livelihoods and essential services. These challenges have heightened the vulnerability of communities to climate-related and other disasters, particularly among women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, internally displaced populations, and other marginalized groups. records.summary: Overview of position Nature of the consultancy: Deliverable Based Consultancy (output-based) Research, data, consultation and in-person facilitation support to the International Consultant for the gender-sensitive Climate Mobility Needs Assessment and Country Diagnostic for Somalia and for the co-creation and validation of the Climate Mobility Programme for integration into the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible. Project Context and Scope: Background Recurrent droughts, floods and environmental degradation, combined with fragility and conflict, drive large-scale human mobility and displacement in Somalia. The National Adaptation Plan (NAP 2.0, 2026–2030) and the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) both recognise human mobility in the context of climate change as a priority. However, limited consolidated data and institutional capacity make it difficult to turn these commitments into investment-ready interventions, and human mobility is not yet well reflected in the NDC 3.0 Investment Plan 2025–2030 launched by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MoECC) at COP 30. In Kenya, HI operates from Nairobi and from field locations including Kakuma and Dadaab, where staff often work in demanding, remote and humanitarian settings that expose them to stress, critical incidents and workplace hazards.
